logic.note: TP4056 states: off below 4 V input, trickle (10 %) below 2.9 V, constant current, constant voltage 4.2 V, full when the current falls below 10 %, recharge below 4.05 V. CHRG / STDBY LEDs follow.

timing.note: State changes are immediate; a finished charge restarts no sooner than 1 s later. Charging speed comes from the battery part (its speedup prop applies).

analog.note: Ideal current source from VIN into BAT clamped at 4.2 V (±10 mV); the real chip is ±1 % on voltage and ±10 % on current, and reduces the current when hot (thermal regulation, often on these modules at 1 A). During CV the input still draws the full set current here.

power.note: Protection (DW01): OUT is cut below 2.4 V and restored above 3.0 V or while charging; it is modelled on the + side, the real module switches the − side. Its ~3 A over-current trip is a warning only.

emulates: CC/CV charge profile with trickle, termination and recharge
USB plug (press) or 5 V on IN+
doesNotEmulate: Thermal regulation (a 1 A module gets hot and slows down)
Load sharing: with a load on OUT while charging, the real chip may never see the end of charge
Battery temperature sensing (TEMP pin is grounded on these modules)
The protection's over-current and short-circuit trip
testOnRealDevice: Set R_PROG for your cell (≤ 1C) before the first charge
How hot the module gets at your charge current
That your device works while charging (load on OUT during CC/CV)
